description: Reconstruct the shared feed-forward input map from scalar groups and test nearest unions
proposal: Family: parameter tying. Current retained frontier is 1,744 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 26 prior macro-attempts and 366 prior micro-trials in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0083/micro-0020 at 1,744 parameters and 99.01%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0081/micro-0007, whose token-matrix union scored 98.97%. Hypothesis: the depth-shared feed-forward input map contains near-duplicate learned scalars independent of the two accepted QKV bands, so reconstructing only this nonlinear feature-construction matrix from scalar groups and greedily unioning its closest values can reduce count without perturbing attention or the FF output map. Ordering is ascending absolute current group-value difference, recomputed after every keep. This parameterization-preserving substitution is more informative than a third QKV band because it tests whether redundancy transfers to a different mechanism while isolating the input side of the FF path. Each micro-trial adds one union and the official runner alone accepts or rolls back. Stop on the first scored discard or error, at the 20-micro-trial cap, or if no pair remains. Compute budget: at most 20 checkpoint migrations and official verifications or 30 wall-clock minutes.
summary: Completed the declared 20 nearest shared feed-forward input scalar unions. All 20 qualified and were retained, moving the frontier from 1,744 parameters at 99.01% to 1,724 parameters at 99.02%; 20 accepts, 0 discards, 0 errors. Pairwise differences rose through 1.888e-4. Compute used checkpoint migration plus 20 official verifications, no fresh optimization, over 24m33s wall clock. Stop reason: fixed 20-micro-trial cap; no scored FF-input boundary was reached.
